# What is Magecart?

by Sansec Forensics Team

Published in Guides − October 31, 2026

A security researcher’s explanation of Magecart, also known as web skimming. The complete history, famous cases, a taxonomy of Magecart attacks, and how to prevent attacks.

## Magecart definition

> Magecart is a type of cybercrime where transaction data is intercepted during the checkout of an online store. Magecart attacks are also known as web skimming, digital skimming or formjacking.

In this article, you will read about the origin of Magecart, a list of famous attacks, a taxonomy of Magecart attack methods, and what you can do to prevent these attacks.

Magecart is still a very active threat to Magento, Adobe Commerce and other ecommerce platforms, Sansecs adds on average 30 malware signatures per day.

We track monthly breaches for the most used platforms.

## Famous Magecart cases

To date, Sansec identified over 70,000 ecommerce websites that suffered a Magecart attack. That is not surprising, since an incredible amount of e-commerce websites run on Magento.

Closing the lid on a Tupperware container is easier than closing the code to Magecart attackers. In 2020 the payment form of the home products was bypassed and visitors were shown a lookalike (”fake payment form”).

The 2021 attack on “The Principality of Sealand” (an abandoned platform 10 kilometers of the coast of Great Britain in the North Sea, that claims independence) could be described as a successful attempt to stop people from buying a Duke or Baron title in a web store.

2022 saw another prominent hack: Segway, maker of the two-wheeled self-balancing personal transporters. Our global Early Breach Detection Network indicates a period of approximately 20 days before the door was finally closed.

【48†🔍 Fix Site Pixel Detection and Auditor Timeouts 🧭 Overview If Search Atlas is not detecting your site pixel — even though another tool confirms it is present in your page header — the issue is almost always related to how and when the pixel loads, or how the site auditor is able to access your site. This article walks you through the most common causes and how to fix them. 🔍 Why Your Pixel May Not Be Detected Search Atlas scans your page to verify the pixel during the site audit process. Several factors can prevent a successful detection even when the pixel is technically installed: - Pixel loads after the page renders (deferred or async loading): If your pixel fires via JavaScript after the initial page load, the auditor may finish scanning before the pixel becomes visible in the DOM. - Tag Manager delays: Pixels deployed through Google Tag Manager or similar tools may not fire during automated scans because trigger conditions (e.g., user interactions, consent acceptance) are not met. - Consent Management Platform (CMP) blocking: If your site uses a cookie consent banner, the pixel may be blocked until a user accepts cookies — something an automated scanner cannot do. - Caching layers serving a pixel-free version: CDN or server-side caching may serve a cached page that was rendered before the pixel was installed. - Geo-blocking or bot protection rules: Firewalls, Cloudflare bot-fight mode, or geo-restrictions may block the Search Atlas scanner before it can read your page content. - Pixel placed outside the <head> tag: The auditor specifically looks for the pixel in the page head. A pixel placed only in the body or footer may not be found. ⚙️ How to Resolve Pixel Detection Issues 1. Confirm placement in the <head> tag: Open your page source (right-click → View Page Source) and confirm the Search Atlas pixel snippet appears inside the <head> section, not just in the body. 2. Switch to direct (non-GTM) installation: Temporarily install the pixel directly in your site's theme or template header file, bypassing Tag Manager, to rule out trigger-condition issues. 3. Disable or configure your CMP for the pixel: Whitelist the Search Atlas pixel in your Consent Management Platform so it loads without requiring user consent, or set it to fire in the pre-consent category. 4. Purge your CDN and server cache: After installing or adjusting the pixel, clear all caching layers so the scanner receives a fresh version of your page. 5. Whitelist the Search Atlas crawler: In your firewall or bot-protection settings, allow automated scanners to access your site. If you use Cloudflare, temporarily disable Bot Fight Mode and retest. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The research summaries, theses, price targets, scanner picks, watcher verdicts, and trade decisions you see are generated in whole or in part by large language models and rule-based heuristics. These systems can:

  * misread fundamentals, news, or filings;

  * produce decisions that look reasonable but are systematically biased.

The auto-trading agent acts on these outputs. You must independently understand and accept the risk that the agent will make decisions you disagree with, including decisions that lose money.
